description:
We are FAST NU computing undergrads taking a shot in making a crazy game about Space Missions in this years NASA Space Apps Hackathon

Wish us good luck
summary: Mission Architect: Pathways to the Stars is an interactive 3D web game that lets players step into the role of astronaut candidates at a fictional space agency to design, manage, and simulate complete space missions from concept to operations. Players define mission objectives across six pathways (Low Earth Orbit, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Interstellar Probe, and Exoplanet Telescope), assemble a 3D spacecraft from real subsystems, select trajectories and launch vehicles, pass an Engineering Review Board, launch, and manage in-flight anomalies and physics challenges. Every choice creates real cross-system trade-offs across budget, mass, power, communications, data, and mission lifetime. By pairing real-time 3D visualization with plain-language explanations, a Mission Notebook, and a post-mission "Why" debrief report, the game makes space systems engineering intuitive, collaborative, and engaging for learners without advanced aerospace backgrounds.
details:
What does it do & how does it work?

- Complete Mission Lifecycle: Players progress through a guided 7-step training prologue, select a mission pathway and contract requirements, assemble a 3D spacecraft in a hangar bay (bus, power, battery, flight computer, attitude control, communications, propulsion, thermal, radiation shielding, life support, and scientific instruments), pass an Engineering Review Board (ERB), pick a trajectory and launch vehicle, complete a GO/NO-GO poll, fly an interactive 3D launch ascent (ignition timing, Max-Q throttle-down, stage/fairing separation, orbit insertion), and manage day-by-day flight operations.

- Systems Trade-Offs & Simulation: Every component and trajectory decision updates 6 constrained resources (budget, mass, power, communications/downlink, data, and lifetime) in real time using simplified SI-unit spaceflight physics (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, orbital velocity, inverse-square solar flux, Hohmann transfers, gravity assists, link budgets, and transit photometry).

- In-Flight Events, Challenges & Team Play: Flights feature random anomalies, physics calculation consoles (including an Exoplanet Transit Light-Curve analyzer), NPC engineer advisor bubbles, and optional 2-4 player hot-seat team voting with role ownership, Commander tie-breaks, and timed negotiation dilemmas.

- Evaluation & Replay: A 3D post-mission report scores performance across weighted criteria, highlights hardware fault/success points on the 3D spacecraft, explains why each design choice succeeded or failed, compares runs side-by-side, and supports MA1: share codes plus one-click Redesign & Re-fly.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Turns abstract orbital mechanics and spacecraft engineering into hands-on cause-and-effect gameplay.

- Includes beginner-friendly Cadet difficulty, contextual Mission Notebook formula cards, procedural Web Audio soundscapes/SFX with live captions, and accessibility modes (Large Text, High Contrast, Reduced Motion, Subtitles).

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & 3D: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Three.js, React Three Fiber, @react-three/drei, Zustand, Immer, Zod.

- Audio & Assets: Procedural Web Audio API synthesizer (soundEngine.ts), NASA 3D Resources .glb models (with Meshopt & local Draco decoders), Solar System Scope 2K planetary textures.

- Testing & Quality: Vitest (236 unit/simulation tests), Playwright (16 end-to-end browser tests across desktop and mobile), ESLint.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

- Keeping the physics grounded and educational without overwhelming non-specialists (plain-language cards + visual trade-off deltas + difficulty presets).

- Ensuring multiple distinct spacecraft architectures can succeed on every pathway rather than forcing a single "correct" answer.

- Maintaining strict agency independence (fictional Orbital Exploration Agency, clear educational disclaimers: Simplified physics for learning / Not to scale).
